The tool fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern build-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as tool coded rather than literal locked-coded shape.

In real-world usage 🔒 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate build-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'tool 🔒' build-marker marker. What separates 🔒 from the rest of the shape family is the tool register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'tool coded locked,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition.
